reply: Guided tour of RW Aurigae: 7 steps. Touch any control to take over.

steps.say: This is RW Aurigae: Young T Tauri star with a disk; its brightness changes irregularly. SPHEREx imaged it on 3 dates in D3, from 2025-09-10 to 2026-09-11 (366 days). The view starts on D3 (1.63–2.41 µm).
Play the dates in order. This object does not move at SPHEREx scale; look at its brightness from one date to the next.
Blink compares two dates directly: 2025-09-10 against 2026-09-11. A moving source jumps; a still one only changes brightness, if at all.

The six detectors cover 0.75–5.0 µm, from left to right. In the measurements it is detected in D1, D2, D3, D4, D5, D6. Its D5/D4 flux ratio (methane index) is 1.7; ordinary stars sit near 0.5–1.5 and methane-rich cold dwarfs far above.
Its flux changes between dates beyond the noise. The difference image 2026-09-11 minus 2025-09-10 shows it: white is brighter in the later date.
The rule-based engine labels it a star; that agrees with the catalog type (star, SIMBAD).
5 of 52 sources in this field need a human look. The first one, Gaia DR3 156430100561810560, is flagged for: Moves, no catalog motion. Is it real or an artefact?
